text:
You want to learn web development by building a clone of a specific web app, including checkout flows for cards and PayPal subscriptions, and you’re looking for someone who can guide you through it while keeping the project practical and affordable.

I’m Tobias Reyne, and with 7 years of experience in JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, full stack development, HTML, and CSS, I can help you build this in a way that teaches you how the pieces fit together rather than just handing over code. Since you already have some coding background and want to understand web apps better, I’d approach this as a collaborative build: we can break the clone into clear milestones, review each part as we go, and make sure you understand the structure, data flow, and checkout logic.

A relevant project I built was a booking platform for fitness studios, where I created a white-label class booking app with subdomains, timetables, and memberships. One result from that project was onboarding 64 studios in 6 months, and Stripe checkout reached a 71% conversion rate. I’ve also rebuilt a home goods storefront into a headless setup using Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, Sanity, and Vercel. In that project, the largest contentful paint improved from 4.1s to 1.3s, which helped the store feel much faster and more polished.

For your project, I’d focus on creating the core web app first, then layering in the checkout and subscription flows. Since you have months for this and are flexible with weekly hours, that gives us room to build it carefully and make it educational. I’m comfortable working from a reference site and translating that into a clean, understandable implementation. I can also help you compare approaches so you learn why certain patterns are better for maintainability.

Given your budget, I’d be happy to discuss a fixed-price structure based on scope so we can keep expectations clear from the start. If the collaboration goes well, I’d also be open to continuing with future paid learning projects.

What parts of the clone are most important for you to understand first: the frontend layout, the database and auth flow, or the Stripe checkout and subscription setup?
